# Security Policy

This is a generalization of the security policies for all projects owned/primarily maintained by:

- [@therealbenpai](https://github.com/therealbenpai) on GitHub
- [@benshawmean](https://gitlab.com/benshawmean) on GitLab

Project-specific policies (if any) will take precedence over this general policy. Please refer to the individual project's documentation for any specific instructions or guidelines.

## Reporting a Vulnerability

If you have found a vulnerability in one of our projects, please report it to me as soon as possible. I take security very seriously and will try to work with you to resolve the issue.

My contact information can be found on my website's [contact page](https://benshawmean.com/contact) and in the repository's `security.txt` file. You can also reach out to me directly on GitHub or GitLab.

When reporting a vulnerability, please provide as much detail as possible, including:

- A clear description of the vulnerability
- Steps to reproduce the issue
- Any relevant screenshots or logs
- The impact of the vulnerability (e.g., potential data loss, unauthorized access, etc.)
- CVSS v3.1 or v4.0 score (if applicable)
- Any associated CVEs or CWEs (if applicable)
- Your contact information (optional, but helpful for follow-up)
- Any suggested fixes or mitigations (if you have any)
- The affected version(s) of the project

## Response Time

Due to me having a substantial amount of work and projects, I may not be able to respond immediately. However, I will do my best to acknowledge receipt of your report within 48 hours and provide updates on the resolution process as needed.

For critical vulnerabilities, I will prioritize the resolution and work to address the issue as quickly as possible. For less critical issues, I will still aim to resolve them in a timely manner, but please understand that it may take longer due to other commitments.

## Disclosure Policy with regards to compensation/bounties

I am a solo developer on most of my projects and do not use them as a source of revenue. Because of that, I am not able to provide any fiscal compensation for vulnerabilities found in these projects. Certain exceptions may be made for critical issues found if I have the ability to provide compensation, but this is not guaranteed and will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis.

I do however try to credit any and all parties who took part in the report. If you would like to be credited for your report, please let me know in your report and provide the name you would like to be credited as. If you would like to remain anonymous, please let me know in your report, and I will respect your privacy.

## Scopes of vulnerabilities

The scope of vulnerabilities that I will accept must relate directly to the project's source code. Issues involving dependencies, third-party services, or other external factors may not be within the scope of this policy. I will still try and fix any issues related to dependencies or third-party services if I am able to, but I cannot guarantee the complete resolution of such issues.

## Thank you

Thank you for taking the time to read this security policy and for your efforts in helping to keep our projects secure. Your contributions are greatly appreciated, and I look forward to working with you to resolve any vulnerabilities that may arise.
